programme.title: Seo BBC ALBA. This is BBC ALBA
programme.desc: Sealladh ùr bho Alba. A new view from Scotland.

programme.title: Boban is Fuigheag
programme.desc: Tha ’ad a' cluich tarraing an ròp an-diugh - no am b’ fheàrr tarraing an clò a-ràdh ris? Tha Fuigheag glè mhath air oir tha e nas làidire na shaoileadh tu. They’re playing tug of war today, or should it be called tug of tweed? Fuigheag is very good at it as he’s stronger than one thinks.

programme.title: Dòtaman
programme.desc: Prògram Dòtaman bho 1990 air cuspair an tractor. Seinnibh an òran ainmeil "An Tractar a th'agamsa 's esan a tha thrang..." cuide ri Donnie agus tha sgeulachd is cleasachd gu leòr eile ri fhaotainnn. Coimheadibh airson Cagnaidh is Crotal, agus bithibh deiseal airson Nelson is Napoleon aig a' ghleoc! A classic treat from the Dotaman archives. Recorded in 1990, the programme explores the topic of the tractor. Sing along with Donnie to the iconic song, look out for furry friends Cagnaidh and Crotal and be prepared to count along with Nelson and Napoleon at the Dotaman clock!

programme.title: Meaban and Moo
programme.desc: Bidh Linda a’ tadhal air a caraidean Meaban is Moo sa bhothan aca gus dùbhlain spòrsail a chur romhpa. Anns a’ phrògram seo tha na rionnagan a’ priobadh a-muigh agus tha Linda ag iarraidh air Meaban is Moo trì rudan ann an cumadh rionnaig a lorg. Tha treallaich gu leòr sa bhothan agus feumaidh iad a dhol a rùraich gus an lorg. Linda visits her friends Meaban and Moo at their hut to set them fun challenges. The stars are twinkling outside and Linda tasks Meaban and Moo with finding three star-shaped items. Their hut is full of junk so they need to have a good rummage!

programme.title: Cleasan Ataidh & Tilidh/The Adventures of Abney & Teal
programme.desc: Tha Àtaidh agus Tilidh a’ peantadh diofar rudan, ach cha pheant Nìp còmhla riutha. Chan fhada gus a bheil iad uile còmhla ri Nìp, oir tha e tinn. Feumaidh iad uile smaoineachadh air dòigh airson cuidhteas fhaighinn dhe na spotan aca. Abney and Teal are painting all sorts of things, but Neep won't take part. Soon everyone joins in with Neep instead. They all need to think of something clever to help them with their spots.

programme.title: Ladybird & Bee/Daolag-bhreac is Seillean
programme.desc: Tha tòrr bhèibidhean beaga daolag-bhreac rim frithealadh an-diugh. There are many ladybird babies to look after today.

programme.title: Dan & Gran
programme.desc: Stan and Gran get the giggles while spotting nature on the Ley, and the lake seems to be giggling back at them! Who is that laughing? Tha Dan is Gran a' cireasail fhad 's a tha 'd a' coimhead nàdar air an Loch, 's tha 'n Loch mar gu bheil e a' cireasail air ais thuca! Cò tha siud a' gàireachdaich?

programme.title: Stòiridh
programme.desc: Sgeulachdan do chlann òga. Tha Martainn Mac an t-Saoir a’ leughadh An Crogall fon Leabaidh. Chaidh an leabhar a sgrìobhadh agus a dhealbhachadh le Judith Kerr agus chaidh eadar-theangachadh dhan Ghàidhlig le Dòmhnall Iain MacLeòid. A bedtime story for young children. Martin MacIntyre reads An Crogall fon Leabaidh, written and illustrated by Judith Kerr, and translated into Gaelic by Donald John Macleod.

programme.title: An Saoghal Droil aig Pol Ploc/The Rubbish World of Dave Spud
programme.desc: Tha Deòrsa air dèideag trèana is rèile a thoirt dhachaigh leis, is tha i mòr gu leòr airson is gun urrainn dhan teaghlach air fad a dhol oirre. Saoil càit’ an toir trèana nam Ploc iad? George has brought home a toy train set big enough for all the family to ride. Where might a trip on Spud railways take them?

programme.title: An Saoghal Droil aig Pol Ploc/The Rubbish World of Dave Spud
programme.desc: Tha Pòl ag òrdanachadh inneal armachd uisge ùr le airgead a fhuair e airson a cho-là-breith, ach ’s e aon-adharcach sona dealrach a tha nochdadh tron phost. Saoil an toir seo dath is aoibhneas dha shaoghal ghreannach? Dave orders a water pistol with his birthday money, but is sent a Happy Sparkle unicorn toy instead. Will it bring joy and sparkle into his grumpy world?

programme.title: Stri
programme.desc: Tha preasantairean CBBC ALBA uabhasach fhèin measail air dùbhlain ach saoil cò shoirbhicheas is Alexa a’ tadhal orra? The CBBC ALBA presenters love a good challenge but who will emerge victorious as Alexa joins them?

programme.title: Run - Private Pet
programme.desc: Children’s drama. A young deaf boy visits his granny and befriends a grumpy neighbour’s dog. Together, they show how communication is not always about words.

programme.title: A’ Chùil
programme.desc: Tha Choirstaidh air ais le prògram eile bhon stiùidio aice, A’ Chùil. Sa phrògram seo bheir I sùil air an neach-ealain ainmeil Andy Warhol agus seallaidh I dhut mar a nì thu dealbh anns an stoidhle aigesan. Choirstaidh is back with another programme from her Studio A’ Chùil. In this programme she takes a look at the famous artist Andy Warhol and she shows you how to make your own picture in his style.

programme.title: Dùbhlain DIY (Instructions Not Included)
programme.desc: Judges set two upcycling-themed challenges to the next three couples as they put their DIY skills to the test.

programme.title: SpeakGaelic
programme.desc: Calum Maclean is on the hunt for a world-famous dish which was created in an Indian restaurant in Glasgow.

programme.title: An Là
programme.desc: Naidheachdan ionadail, nàiseanta is eadar-nàiseanta gach là cuide ri fiosrachadh coimhearsnachd bho BBC ALBA. Local, national and international news and information from BBC ALBA.

programme.title: Garradh Phadruig
programme.desc: Summer is over, but Peter is already preparing for the next growing season. Tha’n samhradh seachad ach tha Pàdruig a’deasachadh airson ràithe fàs na h-ath-bhliadhna.

programme.title: Hebridean Baker - Nordic Islands
programme.desc: Coinneach MacLeod explores the food traditions of Bornholm in Denmark. Tha Coinneach MacLeòid a’ faighinn blasad de chultar a’ bhidhe ann am Bornholm san Danmhairg.

programme.title: Rurachd (Foraging)
programme.desc: Mary Ann Kennedy and Lucy Cooke forage at the shore for razor clams, kelp lasagne and carrageen dessert.

programme.title: Miann na Maighdinn-mara/Mermaid Tales
programme.desc: Tha maighdinn-mhara Innse Gall a’ siubhal gu ceann a deas nan Eilean Siar. The Hebridean Mermaid travels to the southern islands of the Outer Hebrides.

programme.title: Faodail
programme.desc: Tha Tasglann Fhilm Faodail a’ tarraing aire gu filmichean dhùthchasach Innse Gall bho na 1930an gu na 80an, a bha caillte ach a-nis glèidhte don ghinealach ri teachd. Tha bhana Cinema Sgìre Leantainneach a’ siubhal nan eilean, a’ taisbeanadh fhilmichean sna sgìrean ionadail, le cothrom am faicinn air-loidhne air feadh an t-saoghail. Cuirear aithris bheairteach ùr riutha, a’ buntainn ris a’ Ghàidhealtachd, airson luchd-amhairc an là an-diugh. The Faodail Film Archive celebrates lost indigenous film collections from the 1930s to the 1980s in the Outer Hebrides, preserving the archive for future generations. The Cinema Sgìre Continuing mobile cinema van travels the islands, showcasing footage to local communities, making them accessible globally online, and adding rich new narratives relevant to the Gàidhealtachd for contemporary audiences. In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: Machair
programme.desc: Drama Gàidhlig stèidhichte ann an Leòdhas. Gaelic soap set on the Isle of Lewis.

programme.title: Fraochy Bay
programme.desc: Là eile ann a Fraochy Bay agus tha sùilean cuid nas motha nam brù. Is ann caol a tha cuisean do dh'fhactaraidh pàidh Featherby's. Tha am fear leis am bheil e a cruthachadh farpais, feuch de am pàidh ùr a bheir an t-acras air na tha mun cuairt agus a chuireas sgillinn dhan a sporran. It's another day in Fraochy Bay and Featherby's Pie Factory has fallen on hard times. Owner Mr Featherby sets up a contest for one lucky person to choose a new pie flavour in order to boost his sales.

programme.title: Alleluia!
programme.desc: Prògram spioradail le laoidhean, sailm agus leughaidhean bho Coats ann am Pàislig, air a lìbhrigeadh le Iain MacFhionghain. Am measg na seinneadairean bidh Maeve NicFhionghain, Ruairidh Gray agus Iain ‘Costello’ MacÌomhair. Cuideachd, an còisir Binneas fo stiùir John Joe MacNèill. Bidh Iain Eàrdsaidh Mac a’ Mhaoilein a’ meòrachadh air cuspair creideimh le leughadh agus smuain, dàn is seallaidhean spioradail à Tiriodh ann an companachd Dòmhnall Eachann Meek agus seirm adhraidh air a’ phìob bho Chloe Steele à Manachainn nan Lios. Iain MacKinnon presents a mix of hymns, psalms and readings from Coats in Paisley. Amongst the singers performing are Maeve MacKinnon, Ruairidh Gray and Iain ‘Costello’ Maciver. Also appearing is the choir Binneas, conducted by John Joe MacNeil. John Archie MacMillan reflects on his beliefs with a selected reading and thought, spiritual poetry and landscapes in the company of Donald E Meek in Tiree. Chloe Steele performs a tune of worship on the pipes from Beauly Priory. In Gaelic with English subtitles

programme.title: Omnibus
programme.desc: Humphrey Burton examines the golden age of Spanish painting, originally broadcast in 1976 to coincide with a major exhibition at the Royal Academy of Arts.

programme.title: Britain's Lost Waterlands: Escape to Swallows and Amazons Country
programme.desc: Documentary that follows presenters Dick Strawbridge and Alice Roberts as they explore the spectacular British landscapes that inspired children's author Arthur Ransome to write his series Swallows and Amazons. The landscapes he depicted are based on three iconic British waterlands. The beauty and drama of the Lake District shaped by ancient glaciers and rich in wildlife and natural resources, the shallow man-made waterways of the Norfolk broads so crucial to farming and reed production, and the coastal estuaries and deep-water harbours of the Suffolk coastline shaped by ferocious tides and crucial to trade. Engineer and keen sailor Dick uses vintage boats to explore the landscapes and meet people whose lives are shaped by the water, while wildlife enthusiast Alice explores the rich shorelines, interrogating the underlying geography and meeting the wildlife. Together they evoke the nostalgia of Ransome's writing and a bygone era of childhood freedom and adventure, but they also explore the economic significance of these special locations and the ways in which water was harnessed to change the course of British history.

programme.title: Ardal O’Hanlon: Tomb Raider
programme.desc: The story of an epic 1930s quest to find the origins of the earliest Irish men and women on the island of Ireland using archaeology. Ardal goes back to world-famous archaeological sites to see how Ireland had some of the most important finds in Europe at the time. Further beneath the surface, Ardal discovers how both in Northern Ireland and what was then called the Irish Free State, archaeology was being used as an important tool for nation-building, as both states forged new identities in the wake of Partition. He unravels a forgotten time period, when a team of Americans from Harvard University, a Nazi archaeologist from Austria and a Welsh geography professor based in Belfast dug up ancient sites across the country. Their pioneering work laid the foundation for modern archaeology in Ireland, north and south, and yet is largely a forgotten story. Through Ardal’s journey, the film rediscovers this strange 1930s tale but also ends up answering some of Ardal’s deepest questions about the Celts, and ultimately, what it means to be Irish.

programme.title: Kamikaze: An Untold History
programme.desc: On the Pacific front, towards the end of World War II, Japan's imperial armed forces launched 'kamikaze' attacks - suicide missions by aircraft laden with bombs. It was a mad operation with no hope of returning alive, but the nation went wild, and the attacks continued for ten months, literally until the very last day of the war. Close to 4,000 Japanese airmen died, and nearly 7,000 Allied military personnel were killed, and thousands more were injured by the attacks. How could this happen? Utilising 15 years' worth of extensive interviews with US and Japanese World War II veterans, Takayuki Oshima’s film delves into the mechanism of how a crazed madness swept through an entire nation.

programme.title: The Sky at Night
programme.desc: Professor Brian Cox joins the team to explore the mind-bending mysteries of black holes discovered by the James Webb Space Telescope’s most exciting new observations.

programme.desc: Series exploring topical scientific issues. A look at the fledgling field of extraterrestrial meteorology as technology allows astronomers to study other planets in new ways.

programme.title: Talking Business
programme.desc: Can oil really save Venezuela's economy? The country has the world's largest reserves, so can it take advantage whilst global energy supplies are under pressure because of events in the Middle East? Reviving Venezuela's biggest industry is just one part of the change that's needed as the country recovers from deadly earthquakes and tries to restructure a mountain of debt after years of mismanagement. Respected former central bank president Ruth Krivoy and leading oil executive Ali Moshiri of Amos Global Energy give their takes on the role oil can play. Meanwhile, the president of Venezuela's Chambers of Commerce and Industry, Felipe Capozzolo of Fedecamaras, explains some of the other reforms that could help the country become wealthy again.

programme.title: The Climate Question
programme.desc: A global programme that reflects the variety of takes on climate change, how best to understand it and the world's attempts to avert it, temper it or adapt to it. It is not about questioning whether climate change is happening, it's about finding the best ways to respond to it. This is sharp-edged, analytical inquiry. Hard scrutiny, touched with a sense of adventure and discovery, and where we can find it, hope. It includes stories from across the world on why we find it so hard to save our own planet, and how we might change that.

programme.title: Breakfast
programme.desc: The latest news, sport, business and weather from the BBC's Breakfast team.

programme.title: Animal Park
programme.desc: The day has finally arrived for the Longleat's first new hippos in decades to arrive at the park. Sisters Matilda and Manon have come on a 700-mile journey from the Czech Republic. The team have been working for months to prepare their new, state-of-the-art home, but will these nervous giants take the vital first step out of the travel crates? In Lion Country, huge male Klaus’s dominance has been in question after he sustained an injury. To see if he is back to full strength, the keepers have set up an enrichment test – a rope toy attached to a digital gauge and a truck. As Klaus takes the rope in his jaws and starts to pull, we find out if he will be able to remain in charge.

programme.title: Trace, Track, Get My Car Back
programme.desc: A family car fitted with a child seat is stolen off a driveway by car key burglars. But as the heartless thieves make their getaway, tracker Richard is alerted by the vehicle’s tiny tracking device and is quickly hot on their heels. There is a setback when the thieves find the car’s tracker, realising it is transmitting a GPS signal and that they are being followed. They dispose of the tracker, and the trail goes cold, but Richard’s not about to give up. Can he find another way to trace the family’s car and return it to its rightful owners? At Felixstowe Port, stolen vehicle examiner Adam intercepts a suspect shipping container about to leave the country, heading for Africa. Inside, he finds five stolen vehicles, all with false plates to disguise their true identities. In Coventry, former police officer Neil is on the trail of a stolen VW Golf fitted with a satellite tracker. It’s parked in a residential street, but are the thieves lying in wait?

programme.title: European Athletics Championships
programme.desc: Keely Hodgkinson begins the defence of her European title as the women’s 800m gets under way with the qualifying rounds. The Netherlands’ Femke Broeders-Bol and the fastest woman in the world this year, Audrey Werro of Switzerland, are also in action and will provide a tough challenge for Great Britain’s Olympic gold medallist. Qualifying for tonight’s men’s 100m final is also on the track on day 2 of the European Athletics Championships in Birmingham. Jessica Ennis-Hill and Greg Rutherford are in the studio to provide expert analysis alongside Jeanette Kwakye. Steve Cram, Steve Backley, Andrew Cotter, Colin Jackson and Paula Radcliffe are in the commentary box.

programme.title: Money for Nothing
programme.desc: In Greater Manchester, upcycling expert Jacqui Joseph explores the Altrincham recycling centre, hoping to discover unwanted items that can be revamped or revitalised and sold on for cash. She calls on lighting designer Duncan to restore a once-loved retro radio, and can newbie Tyler find a way to save an old sewing machine table?

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: In the Cotswolds, Nicki Chapman and a couple from Scotland don’t need to look too far to find the characterful cottage of their dreams for a £600,000 budget. Whilst in the region, Nicki drops in on showjumping legend and double Olympic gold medallist Nick Skelton, along with his sons Harry and Dan, who are following in their father’s ‘hoof’ prints.

programme.title: Trace, Track, Get My Car Back
programme.desc: A family car fitted with a child seat is stolen off a driveway by car key burglars. But as the heartless thieves make their getaway, tracker Richard is alerted by the vehicle’s tiny tracking device and is quickly hot on their heels. There is a setback when the thieves find the car’s tracker, realising it is transmitting a GPS signal and that they are being followed. They dispose of the tracker, and the trail goes cold, but Richard’s not about to give up. Can he find another way to trace the family’s car and return it to its rightful owners? At Felixstowe Port, stolen vehicle examiner Adam intercepts a suspect shipping container about to leave the country, heading for Africa. Inside, he finds five stolen vehicles, all with false plates to disguise their true identities. In Coventry, former police officer Neil is on the trail of a stolen VW Golf fitted with a satellite tracker. It’s parked in a residential street, but are the thieves lying in wait?

programme.title: European Athletics Championships

programme.title: Trace, Track, Get My Car Back

Inside, he finds five stolen vehicles, all with false plates to disguise their true identities. In Coventry, former police officer Neil is on the trail of a stolen VW Golf fitted with a satellite tracker. It’s parked in a residential street, but are the thieves lying in wait?

programme.title: European Athletics Championships
programme.desc: Keely Hodgkinson begins the defence of her European title as the women’s 800m gets under way with the qualifying rounds. The Netherlands’ Femke Broeders-Bol and the fastest woman in the world this year, Audrey Werro of Switzerland, are also in action and will provide a tough challenge for Great Britain’s Olympic gold medallist. Qualifying for tonight’s men’s 100m final is also on the track on day 2 of the European Athletics Championships in Birmingham. Jessica Ennis-Hill and Greg Rutherford are in the studio to provide expert analysis alongside Jeanette Kwakye. Steve Cram, Steve Backley, Andrew Cotter, Colin Jackson and Paula Radcliffe are in the commentary box.

programme.title: Money for Nothing
programme.desc: In Greater Manchester, upcycling expert Jacqui Joseph explores the Altrincham recycling centre, hoping to discover unwanted items that can be revamped or revitalised and sold on for cash. She calls on lighting designer Duncan to restore a once-loved retro radio, and can newbie Tyler find a way to save an old sewing machine table?

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: In the Cotswolds, Nicki Chapman and a couple from Scotland don’t need to look too far to find the characterful cottage of their dreams for a £600,000 budget. Whilst in the region, Nicki drops in on showjumping legend and double Olympic gold medallist Nick Skelton, along with his sons Harry and Dan, who are following in their father’s ‘hoof’ prints.

programme.title: The Repair Shop
programme.desc: The team rescue a jacket worn by a beloved search dog involved in the Lockerbie disaster, as well as tackle a pair of rugby boots that helped England win the Women’s World Cup.

programme.title: Reporting Scotland
programme.desc: More from the day’s top stories and communities across Scotland.

programme.title: My Kind of Town
programme.desc: In this episode, Ian and Major spend time in the Fife town of Cupar. A traditional market town, Cupar now has ambitions to be a digital town, and Ian finds out from the locals what this means. It’s not all work for Ian, as he gets the chance to practise his swing on the stunning Kingarrock Hickory golf course and sample some tasty morsels at the farmers’ market. He also gets creative in the kitchen at family bakers Fisher and Donaldson, and Major takes time out for some pampering at the grooming parlour.

programme.title: This Farming Life
programme.desc: Filmed across a year, this series follows the lives of five farming families across Scotland. The autumn sales are over, and preparations are being made for winter. In Newtonmore, in the Cairngorms National Park, Robert MacKenzie needs to gather in all his pregnant cows back to the croft for pregnancy testing. Costs of feed and fertiliser have shot up this year, so if not enough are in calf, it may be time to stop farming cattle. In North Uist, the MacDonald family are harvesting potatoes grown in the sandy Machair soil that is unique to the west of Scotland. The croft has been in Angus’s hands since the 1980s, but now he is steadily handing over the reins to son Fraser and daughter-in-law Carianne. On Thorabella Farm in Moray, Nikki and Ollie Lake are doing things a bit differently, having bought their first farm in 2017 with the goal of living as self-sufficiently as possible. They need to call on the vet to help one of their cows that is experiencing a difficult birth.

programme.title: Murder Trial
programme.desc: In 2024, the body of 65-year-old groundsman Brian Low is discovered on a country track in rural Aberfeldy, his beloved black labrador Millie by his side. Police assume that Brian has suffered a medical episode, but six days later, the post-mortem reveals the shocking truth - Brian has been shot dead. His former colleague and gamekeeper on the estate where he worked, David Campbell, now stands trial for his murder. With the site of the murder exposed to the elements for days, police are unable to forensically link anyone to the deceased. The prosecution builds a case against the accused around smaller, individual strands of circumstantial evidence while working to convince the jury that he is guilty beyond reasonable doubt.

programme.title: David Wilson's Crime Files
programme.desc: Criminologist David Wilson charts the origins and evolution of forensic science as an ever-more important tool for crime detection.

programme.title: Tommy: The Good. The Bad. The Fury
programme.desc: Tommy’s childhood friend Chris asks him to do a book reading at the school where they once studied. Tommy faces his nerves and steps up, inspiring students to dream big and believe anything is possible. Tragedy then strikes with the passing of boxing legend Ricky Hatton - a devastating loss for his friends, family and Manchester. Tommy trained with Ricky for 18 months, and his friend and mentor’s passing reminds him how important it is to live life to the fullest. Tommy sets out on the most gruelling test of endurance possible: climbing the three highest mountains in England, Scotland and Wales in just 24 hours. Battling brutal conditions and exhaustion, he pushes through to finish with only minutes to spare, greeted at the summit by an emotional John. At Halloween, Tommy and John go pumpkin picking with Bambi, things are back on track with Molly, and the house renovation is almost completed. He reflects on where he was last autumn and everything he’s achieved over the past year, and looks forward to a brighter future.

programme.title: Drugs Map of Britain
programme.desc: How a local community in Birmingham has been impacted by nitrous oxide, told through the users, the shops that sell it and the activist trying to stop it.

programme.title: Drugs Map of Britain
programme.desc: An unflinching look at young ketamine users in Plymouth, whose consumption has moved away from parties and into their bedrooms, as they use the drug to self-medicate.

programme.title: Drugs Map of Britain
programme.desc: We follow young drug users who have grown up with generational drug use in Fife, where you can get 'half a gram quicker than you can get a taxi.'

programme.title: Drugs Map of Britain
programme.desc: This episode explores the impact of cocaine in London, where users say it’s been normalised.

programme.title: Disclosure Shorts
programme.desc: Around one in seven people in the UK are on antidepressants, but do we know all we need to about the risks and benefits of taking this medication? Anton Ferrie investigates the impact of these pills on the minds and bodies of the thousands of young people who take them and meets those for whom their use has had profound consequences. Some say these drugs have saved their lives; others that they’ve changed them permanently, wiping out their sex lives and numbing them to the world around them.

programme.title: BBC Comedy Short Films
programme.desc: This is an average story of a very average woman. Of Spud, carer for her father, who cooks, cleans and serves badly and half-heartedly. A woman who is never seen or thanked. Ignored. A woman who, in spite of what society tells her, does not feel bad about herself. Who despite not being young, or a mother, or worst of all, beautiful, is actually quite happy in herself, if not her life. Then, one day, everything changes, and Siobhan may have to come out of the shadows and be seen.

programme.title: Lara Croft: Tomb Raider
programme.desc: Action tale, adapted from the popular video game, in which the eponymous heroine races against time to find an ancient relic before it falls into the wrong hands. Leaving behind her life of luxury, the highly trained adventurer travels to exotic and dangerous locales, where she battles a variety of fantastical creatures in the knowledge that the fate of mankind rests in her hands.

programme.title: RuPaul's Drag Race UK
programme.desc: The time has come to meet a brand new set of racers! In this extra-special preview, RuPaul invites you to meet the 12 fabulous new hopefuls who are revving their engines ready to snatch the crown and the coveted title of the UK’s Next Drag Race Superstar.

programme.title: Bridget Jones's Diary
programme.desc: Romantic comedy telling the story of a neurotic thirty-something who resolves to take control of her life once and for all. She drinks, smokes and eats too much, and, worst of all, she falls for the wrong kind of man - passing over Mr Right for Mr Right Now. From the novel by Helen Fielding.

programme.title: Bridget Jones: The Edge of Reason
programme.desc: Bridget Jones finds happiness but then questions if she really does have everything she ever wanted.

programme.title: Matthew Perry and the Ketamine Queen
programme.desc: Documentary investigating events leading up to the shocking death of Friends star Matthew Perry and the woman at the centre of the case, dubbed the 'Ketamine Queen' by US prosecutors. Jasveen Sangha, a drug dealer and dual US-UK citizen, has pleaded guilty to five federal charges in Los Angeles, including one count of distributing ketamine resulting in death or bodily injury. She faces up to 65 years in prison for supplying Perry with the drugs that led to his death. Sangha was one of five people charged in the case. Prosecutors described her home as a 'drug-selling emporium', where authorities found approximately 79 vials of ketamine and other drugs, including methamphetamine, cocaine and Xanax. Presented by Amber Haque, the film features exclusive, first-on-the-record interviews with Sangha's friends and examines her role in Perry’s death and Hollywood’s ketamine drug network.

programme.title: Bergerac
programme.desc: The battle between Bergerac and Arthur Wakefield intensifies as his enemies gain ground. Since discovering that Cate may have betrayed Arthur, Bergerac feels he is closing in on his chief suspect. But a storm is gathering, with Chloe’s expose gaining momentum when she finds new evidence against him that indicates there may be some truth in John Blakely’s accusations after all. Meanwhile, there’s a huge surprise in store when the missing money from the ransom appears.

programme.title: This is BBC Two
programme.desc: Highlights of programmes on BBC Two.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: A former pastry chef in Norfolk turns his attention to property development. In Liverpool, a new owner brings her design perspective to a one-bedroom flat. And in Birmingham, Martin is left to figure out whether it’s a leasehold or a freehold at his property.

programme.title: Money for Nothing
programme.desc: Are old plates valuable? It's a smashing skip find for Sarah Moore at Witley recycling centre in Surrey, but can she find a way to release the cash from this collection of china? Carpenter Ollie tries to launder a tidy profit from an old washstand, and husband and wife team Dani and Elliot have their hands full with sad seats in need of some TLC.

programme.title: The Great British Sewing Bee
programme.desc: The ten remaining sewers celebrate the rich fashion and textile traditions of Mexico. Host Sophie Willan and judges Patrick Grant and Esme Young are joined by a special guest judge, renowned fashion designer Erika Alvirez. In the Pattern Challenge, the sewers create a Mexican folkloric top using fabrics created by indigenous communities in Mexico’s Oaxaca region. For the Transformation Challenge, they are given manteles de hule, a traditional Mexican tablecloth. Using the stiffness of the fabric, they are asked to create a garment with an eye-catching structure. Finally, in the Made-to-Measure, the sewers design an outfit inspired by one of the many Mexican festivals found across the country.

programme.title: BBC News
programme.desc: Twenty-four hours a day, the latest national and international stories as they break.

programme.title: Antiques Road Trip
programme.desc: Margie Cooper, Tim Medhurst and their electric-powered fire engine, Sam, make their way to Liverpool. They scour the city for secrets but still find time for a bit of moving meditation in Europe's first Chinatown. Tim sets a dining table at the auction, while Margie opts for a more industrial haul.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: Two brothers argue over who’ll be getting the biggest bedroom in Stoke, some textured walls in Cannock have Dion raising his eyebrows, while Martel is on home turf in Scotland, where dad is taking the lead from his youngest daughter!

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Christina Trevanion and the teams are in Nottinghamshire, hunting for antiques to sell on for a profit. Experts Philip Serrell and Roo Irvine lend a hand before they all head to Bishton Hall in Staffordshire for the auction. Christina discovers how a young girl once sowed the seeds of one of Britain’s most popular apples.

programme.title: Richard Osman's House of Games
programme.desc: Every day this week, celebrity contestants Mehreen Baig, Clare Balding, Jamie Laing and Mike Wozniak take on a series of quiz rounds selected by the host, quiz legend Richard Osman. A daily winner is declared following a quickfire round at the end of each show, and the scores are tallied across the week, resulting in an overall champion being crowned on Friday. Will the winning stars opt for the much-coveted House of Games wheelie luggage, or will they be tempted by the House of Games reusable coffee mug, which is brand new for this series?

programme.title: The Finish Line
programme.desc: Roman Kemp and his sidekick Sarah Greene host this quiz show, where the contestants race on moving podiums across the studio floor. Correct answers get the players moving, while wrong answers stop them in their tracks. Five contestants battle across a series of fast-paced qualifiers and head-to-head races, where the aim of the game is simple – make it to the finish line before your rivals. The winner then races against the track itself in an attempt to win the £5,000 cash prize.

programme.title: Do You Know Your Place?
programme.desc: The competition intensifies as the celebrity trio, EastEnders star Nitin Ganatra, the Rev Kate Bottley and Alex Gray, aka Apollo from Gladiators, return for day 2. Vernon Kay keeps order as the quiz master, while sidekick Paul Gorton takes the contestants on a tour of today’s destination, Dudley. The race to the weekly finale is well and truly on.

programme.title: The Farmers' Country Showdown
programme.desc: Friends and livestock farming duo Ian and Luke are passionate about producing high quality meat, and a vital location for selling it is Guildford Farmers’ Market in Surrey. Ian is keen to use his hospitality background, attracting customers with cooking advice, and hopes that the warm weather will bring out the barbecuing buyers. This market is also important for John, a third-generation Sussex fruit farmer. As well as picking his finest fresh fruit, he also makes apple juice so he can pocket as many sales as possible. With over 1,000 customers expected, the farmers hope it will be a lucrative day away from their jobs at the farm.

programme.title: Spy in the Ocean
programme.desc: Spy Creatures explore animal emotions, showing the deep feelings we share. With surfing dolphins, kissing manatees and sensitive cuttlefish, it’s an amazing, emotional rollercoaster.

programme.title: Antiques Roadshow
programme.desc: On a visit to Sherborne School in Dorset the experts make exciting finds including an inflatable paper globe dating from 1830, a George Cross and a George Medal awarded to the same man for his work in bomb disposal, a Patek Philippe pocket watch of great value and a collection of work by EH Shepard, the illustrator of Winnie the Pooh. Michael Aspel is intrigued to open a First World War pigeon post message container thought to contain an important message.

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: The show comes from Milestones Museum in Basingstoke, which recreates the streets of Hampshire past. Elizabeth Talbot and James Lewis are the experts doing the honours as they find the best antiques and collectables to take to auction. Meanwhile, Paul Martin meets a modern sculptor who takes nature as his inspiration, carving everything from scorpions to giant spiders.

programme.title: Richard Osman's House of Games
programme.desc: Every day this week, celebrity contestants Chris Bisson, Danielle Harold, Katharine Merry and Robert Webb take on a series of quiz rounds selected by the host, quiz legend Richard Osman. A daily winner is declared following a quickfire round at the end of each show, and the scores are tallied across the week, resulting in an overall champion being crowned on Friday. Will the winning stars opt for the much-coveted House of Games decanter, or will they be tempted by the House of Games retro bag?

programme.title: Bear Grylls - Wild Reckoning
programme.desc: Trish and her husband Byron are falling out over how to parent their big, blended family. They have very different approaches and a 22-year age gap between them – with only a few months age difference between Byron and Trish’s eldest son? The pair take on a blindfolded river walk to get to camp. Then for their second challenge, Byron is in the driving seat. He must decide which of them climbs a stack of crates and which climbs a rope ladder, before they both make a leap of faith for a reward. In their campfire chat, mediator Dave gets to the heart of their parenting clashes and helps them find a way to carve out time for themselves amidst the chaos of busy family life. Can they learn how to present a united front to the children? Or will their parenting clashes drive them apart?

programme.title: European Athletics Championships
programme.desc: The evening session on day two of the European Athletics Championships gets underway with the men’s hammer final and qualifying for the women’s pole vault. Innes FitzGerald, Hannah Nuttall and India Weir are all in action in the final of the women’s 5,000m for the British team. London 2012 champions Jessica Ennis-Hill and Greg Rutherford are alongside Gabby Logan in the studio with commentary from Steve Cram, Steve Backley, Andrew Cotter, Colin Jackson and Paula Radcliffe.

programme.title: The Great British Sewing Bee
programme.desc: It's Week 5, and the sewers are tackling the wide world of sport. In the Pattern Challenge, they hit the beach to create classic men’s swimming shorts. The Transformation Challenge sees yet another Sewing Bee first, as the remaining eight sewers are divided into pairs for the first ever team challenge: working together to create outfits from recycled windsurf sails. Finally, the sewers are aiming for a strike as they use free motion embroidery and applique to personalise their made-to-measure bowling shirts.

programme.title: Lucy Worsley Investigates
programme.desc: Mary Tudor, King Henry VIII’s eldest daughter, came to the throne in 1553 and became infamous as one of the bloodiest queens in history. Allegedly executing her subjects at will for their religious beliefs, Mary’s reign became defined by her staunch Catholicism. Lucy Worsley investigates whether England’s first ruling female monarch, Mary I, was truly as ‘bloody’ as history suggests, or whether this reputation arose from being the first woman in a predominantly male world.

programme.title: Interview with the Vampire
programme.desc: Daniel’s probing triggers a troubled Lestat, reminding him of his maker and a lost love, while Louis takes belated revenge.

programme.title: Interview with the Vampire
programme.desc: Haunted by his complicated past, Lestat lies to Daniel and lords it over Armand, while Louis worries his waitress.

programme.title: Uncanny
programme.desc: As a teenager, growing up in a pit community in County Durham, Ian experienced phenomena that seemed to defy rational explanation. He believes his house was haunted by an entity which would shake drawers, ring bells and even flush the toilet. And Ian wasn’t the only person to witness strange things in the house. But could there be a scientific explanation for all this? With help from Dr Ciarán O’Keeffe and Evelyn Hollow, Danny investigates Bearpark’s industrial history, the science of sleep paralysis, and the mechanics of a flushing toilet. His quest for answers even takes him deep into the earth, into an abandoned mine shaft.

programme.title: Bergerac
programme.desc: The battle between Bergerac and Arthur Wakefield intensifies as his enemies gain ground. Since discovering that Cate may have betrayed Arthur, Bergerac feels he is closing in on his chief suspect. But a storm is gathering, with Chloe’s expose gaining momentum when she finds new evidence against him that indicates there may be some truth in John Blakely’s accusations after all. Meanwhile, there’s a huge surprise in store when the missing money from the ransom appears.

programme.title: This is BBC Two
programme.desc: Highlights of programmes on BBC Two.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: A former pastry chef in Norfolk turns his attention to property development. In Liverpool, a new owner brings her design perspective to a one-bedroom flat. And in Birmingham, Martin is left to figure out whether it’s a leasehold or a freehold at his property.

programme.title: Money for Nothing
programme.desc: Are old plates valuable? It's a smashing skip find for Sarah Moore at Witley recycling centre in Surrey, but can she find a way to release the cash from this collection of china? Carpenter Ollie tries to launder a tidy profit from an old washstand, and husband and wife team Dani and Elliot have their hands full with sad seats in need of some TLC.

programme.title: The Great British Sewing Bee
programme.desc: The ten remaining sewers celebrate the rich fashion and textile traditions of Mexico. Host Sophie Willan and judges Patrick Grant and Esme Young are joined by a special guest judge, renowned fashion designer Erika Alvirez. In the Pattern Challenge, the sewers create a Mexican folkloric top using fabrics created by indigenous communities in Mexico’s Oaxaca region. For the Transformation Challenge, they are given manteles de hule, a traditional Mexican tablecloth. Using the stiffness of the fabric, they are asked to create a garment with an eye-catching structure. Finally, in the Made-to-Measure, the sewers design an outfit inspired by one of the many Mexican festivals found across the country.

programme.title: BBC News
programme.desc: Twenty-four hours a day, the latest national and international stories as they break.

programme.title: Antiques Road Trip
programme.desc: Margie Cooper, Tim Medhurst and their electric-powered fire engine, Sam, make their way to Liverpool. They scour the city for secrets but still find time for a bit of moving meditation in Europe's first Chinatown. Tim sets a dining table at the auction, while Margie opts for a more industrial haul.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: Two brothers argue over who’ll be getting the biggest bedroom in Stoke, some textured walls in Cannock have Dion raising his eyebrows, while Martel is on home turf in Scotland, where dad is taking the lead from his youngest daughter!

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Christina Trevanion and the teams are in Nottinghamshire, hunting for antiques to sell on for a profit. Experts Philip Serrell and Roo Irvine lend a hand before they all head to Bishton Hall in Staffordshire for the auction. Christina discovers how a young girl once sowed the seeds of one of Britain’s most popular apples.

programme.title: Richard Osman's House of Games
programme.desc: Every day this week, celebrity contestants Mehreen Baig, Clare Balding, Jamie Laing and Mike Wozniak take on a series of quiz rounds selected by the host, quiz legend Richard Osman. A daily winner is declared following a quickfire round at the end of each show, and the scores are tallied across the week, resulting in an overall champion being crowned on Friday. Will the winning stars opt for the much-coveted House of Games wheelie luggage, or will they be tempted by the House of Games reusable coffee mug, which is brand new for this series?

programme.title: The Finish Line
programme.desc: Roman Kemp and his sidekick Sarah Greene host this quiz show, where the contestants race on moving podiums across the studio floor. Correct answers get the players moving, while wrong answers stop them in their tracks. Five contestants battle across a series of fast-paced qualifiers and head-to-head races, where the aim of the game is simple – make it to the finish line before your rivals. The winner then races against the track itself in an attempt to win the £5,000 cash prize.

programme.title: Do You Know Your Place?
programme.desc: The competition intensifies as the celebrity trio, EastEnders star Nitin Ganatra, the Rev Kate Bottley and Alex Gray, aka Apollo from Gladiators, return for day 2. Vernon Kay keeps order as the quiz master, while sidekick Paul Gorton takes the contestants on a tour of today’s destination, Dudley. The race to the weekly finale is well and truly on.

programme.title: The Farmers' Country Showdown
programme.desc: Friends and livestock farming duo Ian and Luke are passionate about producing high quality meat, and a vital location for selling it is Guildford Farmers’ Market in Surrey. Ian is keen to use his hospitality background, attracting customers with cooking advice, and hopes that the warm weather will bring out the barbecuing buyers. This market is also important for John, a third-generation Sussex fruit farmer. As well as picking his finest fresh fruit, he also makes apple juice so he can pocket as many sales as possible. With over 1,000 customers expected, the farmers hope it will be a lucrative day away from their jobs at the farm.

programme.title: Spy in the Ocean
programme.desc: Spy Creatures explore animal emotions, showing the deep feelings we share. With surfing dolphins, kissing manatees and sensitive cuttlefish, it’s an amazing, emotional rollercoaster.

programme.title: Antiques Roadshow
programme.desc: On a visit to Sherborne School in Dorset the experts make exciting finds including an inflatable paper globe dating from 1830, a George Cross and a George Medal awarded to the same man for his work in bomb disposal, a Patek Philippe pocket watch of great value and a collection of work by EH Shepard, the illustrator of Winnie the Pooh. Michael Aspel is intrigued to open a First World War pigeon post message container thought to contain an important message.

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: The show comes from Milestones Museum in Basingstoke, which recreates the streets of Hampshire past. Elizabeth Talbot and James Lewis are the experts doing the honours as they find the best antiques and collectables to take to auction. Meanwhile, Paul Martin meets a modern sculptor who takes nature as his inspiration, carving everything from scorpions to giant spiders.

programme.title: Richard Osman's House of Games
programme.desc: Every day this week, celebrity contestants Chris Bisson, Danielle Harold, Katharine Merry and Robert Webb take on a series of quiz rounds selected by the host, quiz legend Richard Osman. A daily winner is declared following a quickfire round at the end of each show, and the scores are tallied across the week, resulting in an overall champion being crowned on Friday. Will the winning stars opt for the much-coveted House of Games decanter, or will they be tempted by the House of Games retro bag?

programme.title: Bear Grylls - Wild Reckoning
programme.desc: Trish and her husband Byron are falling out over how to parent their big, blended family. They have very different approaches and a 22-year age gap between them – with only a few months age difference between Byron and Trish’s eldest son? The pair take on a blindfolded river walk to get to camp. Then for their second challenge, Byron is in the driving seat. He must decide which of them climbs a stack of crates and which climbs a rope ladder, before they both make a leap of faith for a reward. In their campfire chat, mediator Dave gets to the heart of their parenting clashes and helps them find a way to carve out time for themselves amidst the chaos of busy family life. Can they learn how to present a united front to the children? Or will their parenting clashes drive them apart?

programme.title: European Athletics Championships
programme.desc: The evening session on day two of the European Athletics Championships gets underway with the men’s hammer final and qualifying for the women’s pole vault. Innes FitzGerald, Hannah Nuttall and India Weir are all in action in the final of the women’s 5,000m for the British team. London 2012 champions Jessica Ennis-Hill and Greg Rutherford are alongside Gabby Logan in the studio with commentary from Steve Cram, Steve Backley, Andrew Cotter, Colin Jackson and Paula Radcliffe.

programme.title: The Great British Sewing Bee
programme.desc: It's Week 5, and the sewers are tackling the wide world of sport. In the Pattern Challenge, they hit the beach to create classic men’s swimming shorts. The Transformation Challenge sees yet another Sewing Bee first, as the remaining eight sewers are divided into pairs for the first ever team challenge: working together to create outfits from recycled windsurf sails. Finally, the sewers are aiming for a strike as they use free motion embroidery and applique to personalise their made-to-measure bowling shirts.

programme.title: Uncanny
programme.desc: As a teenager, growing up in a pit community in County Durham, Ian experienced phenomena that seemed to defy rational explanation. programme.title: Money for Nothing

programme.title: The Great British Sewing Bee
programme.desc: The ten remaining sewers celebrate the rich fashion and textile traditions of Mexico. Host Sophie Willan and judges Patrick Grant and Esme Young are joined by a special guest judge, renowned fashion designer Erika Alvirez. In the Pattern Challenge, the sewers create a Mexican folkloric top using fabrics created by indigenous communities in Mexico’s Oaxaca region. For the Transformation Challenge, they are given manteles de hule, a traditional Mexican tablecloth. Using the stiffness of the fabric, they are asked to create a garment with an eye-catching structure. Finally, in the Made-to-Measure, the sewers design an outfit inspired by one of the many Mexican festivals found across the country.

programme.title: Richard Osman's House of Games
programme.desc: Every day this week, celebrity contestants Mehreen Baig, Clare Balding, Jamie Laing and Mike Wozniak take on a series of quiz rounds selected by the host, quiz legend Richard Osman. A daily winner is declared following a quickfire round at the end of each show, and the scores are tallied across the week, resulting in an overall champion being crowned on Friday. Will the winning stars opt for the much-coveted House of Games wheelie luggage, or will they be tempted by the House of Games reusable coffee mug, which is brand new for this series?

programme.title: The Finish Line
programme.desc: Roman Kemp and his sidekick Sarah Greene host this quiz show, where the contestants race on moving podiums across the studio floor. Correct answers get the players moving, while wrong answers stop them in their tracks. Five contestants battle across a series of fast-paced qualifiers and head-to-head races, where the aim of the game is simple – make it to the finish line before your rivals. The winner then races against the track itself in an attempt to win the £5,000 cash prize.

programme.title: Do You Know Your Place?
programme.desc: The competition intensifies as the celebrity trio, EastEnders star Nitin Ganatra, the Rev Kate Bottley and Alex Gray, aka Apollo from Gladiators, return for day 2. Vernon Kay keeps order as the quiz master, while sidekick Paul Gorton takes the contestants on a tour of today’s destination, Dudley. The race to the weekly finale is well and truly on.

programme.title: The Farmers' Country Showdown
programme.desc: Friends and livestock farming duo Ian and Luke are passionate about producing high quality meat, and a vital location for selling it is Guildford Farmers’ Market in Surrey. Ian is keen to use his hospitality background, attracting customers with cooking advice, and hopes that the warm weather will bring out the barbecuing buyers. This market is also important for John, a third-generation Sussex fruit farmer. As well as picking his finest fresh fruit, he also makes apple juice so he can pocket as many sales as possible. With over 1,000 customers expected, the farmers hope it will be a lucrative day away from their jobs at the farm.

programme.title: Spy in the Ocean
programme.desc: Spy Creatures explore animal emotions, showing the deep feelings we share. With surfing dolphins, kissing manatees and sensitive cuttlefish, it’s an amazing, emotional rollercoaster.

programme.title: Antiques Roadshow
programme.desc: On a visit to Sherborne School in Dorset the experts make exciting finds including an inflatable paper globe dating from 1830, a George Cross and a George Medal awarded to the same man for his work in bomb disposal, a Patek Philippe pocket watch of great value and a collection of work by EH Shepard, the illustrator of Winnie the Pooh. Michael Aspel is intrigued to open a First World War pigeon post message container thought to contain an important message.

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: The show comes from Milestones Museum in Basingstoke, which recreates the streets of Hampshire past. Elizabeth Talbot and James Lewis are the experts doing the honours as they find the best antiques and collectables to take to auction. Meanwhile, Paul Martin meets a modern sculptor who takes nature as his inspiration, carving everything from scorpions to giant spiders.

programme.title: Richard Osman's House of Games
programme.desc: Every day this week, celebrity contestants Chris Bisson, Danielle Harold, Katharine Merry and Robert Webb take on a series of quiz rounds selected by the host, quiz legend Richard Osman. A daily winner is declared following a quickfire round at the end of each show, and the scores are tallied across the week, resulting in an overall champion being crowned on Friday. Will the winning stars opt for the much-coveted House of Games decanter, or will they be tempted by the House of Games retro bag?

programme.title: Bear Grylls - Wild Reckoning
programme.desc: Trish and her husband Byron are falling out over how to parent their big, blended family. They have very different approaches and a 22-year age gap between them – with only a few months age difference between Byron and Trish’s eldest son? The pair take on a blindfolded river walk to get to camp. Then for their second challenge, Byron is in the driving seat. He must decide which of them climbs a stack of crates and which climbs a rope ladder, before they both make a leap of faith for a reward. In their campfire chat, mediator Dave gets to the heart of their parenting clashes and helps them find a way to carve out time for themselves amidst the chaos of busy family life. Can they learn how to present a united front to the children? Or will their parenting clashes drive them apart?

programme.title: European Athletics Championships
programme.desc: The evening session on day two of the European Athletics Championships gets underway with the men’s hammer final and qualifying for the women’s pole vault. Innes FitzGerald, Hannah Nuttall and India Weir are all in action in the final of the women’s 5,000m for the British team. London 2012 champions Jessica Ennis-Hill and Greg Rutherford are alongside Gabby Logan in the studio with commentary from Steve Cram, Steve Backley, Andrew Cotter, Colin Jackson and Paula Radcliffe.

programme.title: The Great British Sewing Bee
programme.desc: It's Week 5, and the sewers are tackling the wide world of sport. In the Pattern Challenge, they hit the beach to create classic men’s swimming shorts. The Transformation Challenge sees yet another Sewing Bee first, as the remaining eight sewers are divided into pairs for the first ever team challenge: working together to create outfits from recycled windsurf sails. Finally, the sewers are aiming for a strike as they use free motion embroidery and applique to personalise their made-to-measure bowling shirts.

programme.title: Lucy Worsley Investigates
programme.desc: Mary Tudor, King Henry VIII’s eldest daughter, came to the throne in 1553 and became infamous as one of the bloodiest queens in history. Allegedly executing her subjects at will for their religious beliefs, Mary’s reign became defined by her staunch Catholicism. Lucy Worsley investigates whether England’s first ruling female monarch, Mary I, was truly as ‘bloody’ as history suggests, or whether this reputation arose from being the first woman in a predominantly male world.

programme.title: American Dad!
programme.desc: US animated comedy series. When Stan sells off the coveted family plot, the Smiths open their own cemetery in their backyard with the help of basketball Hall of Famer Scottie Pippen.

programme.title: Bob's Burgers
programme.desc: Animated comedy about Bob Belcher, who runs Bob's Burgers restaurant, and his family. A massive snowstorm traps the Belchers at home with no working heat as Bob struggles to contact a repairman while warmth-seeking Gene and Louise perfect the art of the living room blanket fort - meanwhile, Tina attempts to clear her name when she believes that another student has accused her of cheating during a test.

programme.title: Bob's Burgers
programme.desc: Animated comedy about Bob Belcher, who runs Bob's Burgers restaurant, and his family. Bob joins Teddy in trying to catch home run balls on his boat floating outside Wonder Wharf Stadium while Linda is left alone to manage the restaurant - elsewhere, Tina and Zeke go to watch when Jimmy Jr takes modern dance lessons at the recreation centre with an overbearing dance instructor.

programme.title: Plebs
programme.desc: Sitcom about three desperate young men who reside in ancient Rome. Grumio meets Justin - the father who left him on a hill as a baby and who now wants to make up for lost time - Stylax starts dating Camilla, a female discus thrower, amidst a sex ban during the Games, and Marcus and Delphine come to terms with their respective pasts.

programme.title: Deep Fake Neighbour Wars
programme.desc: Impressions show that uses deep fake technology to turn the UK's best new impressionists into the world's most famous celebrities. Rihanna and baby Kevin Hart live happily together beside Usain Bolt until his girlfriend - Phoebe Waller-Bridge - arrives on the scene... meanwhile, Adele's awning is under attack from neighbour Jake Paul's pigeons.

programme.title: This Is ITV2+1
programme.desc: Programmes start at 7am. For the full ITV2 schedule, please go to ITV2 on Freeview channel 6.

programme.title: Backyard Builds
programme.desc: Home improvement programme where contractor Brian McCourt and designer Sarah Keenleyside help to expand living spaces by tapping into people's backyards. Amy and Terry love nothing more than spending time outside with their daughters, so Brian and Sarah build a dream enclosure for them to hang out in on summer nights that comes with a swimming pool change room and a new deck where Terry can grill.

programme.title: Dress To Impress
programme.desc: Three single lads are hoping to win the heart of singer and social media handler Emily - gas pipe fitter Anthony, lifeguard Kai, and bodybuilding banker Sol are competing in a shopping challenge in Manchester and searching for the perfect outfit to win a date. Which of the three guys will Dress to Impress?

programme.title: The Real Housewives of Salt Lake City
programme.desc: US reality series peeking inside the unconventional lives of six successful women living in or around Salt Lake City, Utah. The reunion concludes with an emotional update from Bronwyn on her relationship with her mother and marriage to Todd. Lisa and Whitney are brought to tears over their own marriages. Bronwyn confronts Meredith about their off-camera conversation in Greece. After a tumultuous season, the women try to find ways to move forward.

programme.title: The Real Housewives of Orange County
programme.desc: Reality show following the lavish lifestyles of five 'housewives' and their families. The 19th series reunion continues with the ladies questioning Tamra's intentions around sharing Jenn's old photo, Gina addressing comments about Heather's career, Jenn getting a phone call from Ryan revealing shocking information about Katie, and Matt Ginella joining the group in an explosive game of He Said, She Said.

programme.title: The Only Way is Essex
programme.desc: It's Amber's birthday, and Dan has arranged for a surprise getaway with her nearest and dearest - including Amber's pals Mia and Hannah - when Mia reveals that Hannah has a crush on Gatsby. Will sparks fly between the pair? Elsewhere, Dani who is fuming at an Insta video in which Courtney, Chloe M and Gatsby blatantly dig her out - Dani is determined to find out why the girl band have such an issue with her and assumes that Gatsby has been blaming her for his feud with them. Despite the positive vibes at the Be Well Not Jel festival, Dani and Junaid go head to head with Courtney and Chloe M - will Dani get the answers she is looking for, or will things become even more heated and awkward than they were before? Things between Ella and Pete, meanwhile, seem to be progressing well, especially as Pete has found a real connection... with Ella's stepdad Mark - Jordan, on the other hand, is having a heart-to-heart with his mum about her recent cancer diagnosis.

programme.title: Dawson's Creek
programme.desc: US drama series charting the ups and downs of adolescence as experienced by a group of precocious teenagers. The frustration of being stuck in detention on a Saturday morning proves too much for Dawson and his friends - as they become frustrated, they begin to take out their anger on each other in a series of tense exchanges.

programme.title: Charmed
programme.desc: Classic US supernatural drama about three sisters who fight the forces of evil using their combined power of witchcraft known as the Power of Three. Phoebe and Piper vie for Leo's attention as a troubled teenager befriends Phoebe in the hope of joining the Halliwells - unfortunately, the sisters do not realise that she is under the control of a sorceress called Kali who is bent on gaining the girls' powers from them.

programme.title: Deal or No Deal
programme.desc: Join Stephen Mulhern as Jackie takes a shot at winning a life-changing 100,000 pounds - she may be convinced to leave the game early or bravely hold out until the end and be rewarded.

programme.title: Supermarket Sweep
programme.desc: Rylan Clark-Neal hosts the iconic game show as three pairs of shoppers go wild in the aisles and compete in the ultimate supermarket challenge to win a 3,000-pound prize - along with the classic Supermarket Sweep quizzes, trolley dashes and pastel jumpers, the revamped show features exciting new games, challenges and some famous faces.

programme.title: The Floor US
programme.desc: Rob Lowe hosts the American version of the game show. The final players compete for a life-changing victory and the winner is crowned.

programme.title: The Only Way is Essex
programme.desc: After the Be Well Not Jel festival ended in calamity rather than calm, Dani is more convinced than ever that Gatsby has blamed her for the fallout with Chloe M and Courtney. If this wasn't enough, the news of Gatsby kissing new girl Hannah has made its way to Dani... in spite of a pact they made when they split up not to flaunt any new love interests in front of each other. Will things come to a head when they all descend onto the shores of sunny Southend? Love is most definitely in the air with a new couple on the horizon - Chloe B and Jordan Brooks - but what will Chloe's archenemy Ella make of it as the pair meet up for a date in Southend? It's only a few weeks since Jordan took Ella on a date, but will Ella be too busy with a certain Pete Wicks to even care? Meanwhile, Harry decides that he finally needs to learn to drive - his first stop is the theory test, though he has a rather questionable teacher in the form of his cousin Amy Childs.

programme.title: The Real Housewives of Potomac
programme.desc: Reality series following six women living in Potomac, Maryland, a suburb of Washington D.C. and one of the most affluent towns in the United States. Gizelle has a new love interest, Ashley has a new house, and Mia has a new lifestyle - as rumours of Juan's alleged infidelity return but he stands firm on his innocence, Gizelle has no choice but to confront her BFF when Robyn chooses to remain by Juan's side.

programme.title: The Real Housewives of Orange County
programme.desc: Reality show following the lavish lifestyles of five 'housewives' and their families. The 19th series reunion concludes with a heated face-off between Tamra and Gretchen as the group discuss discrepancies surrounding the final dinner in Amsterdam, Emily and Tamra debating the authenticity of their friendship, and emotions running at an all-time high as the ladies react to seeing the footage from the series finale for the first time and leave Tamra in a position that has everyone questioning her integrity.

programme.title: Celebrity Catchphrase
programme.desc: Stephen Mulhern hosts a celebrity special of the classic game show with Kate Garraway, Pete Wicks, and Sir Bradley Wiggins all trying to 'say what they see' as they guess well-known phrases for the chance to win a 50,000-pound jackpot for their chosen charity.

programme.title: The Floor
programme.desc: Rob Brydon hosts the high-stakes and fast-paced game show where 81 contestants battle it out over tense trivia duels to try to conquer The Floor and win £50,000.

programme.title: The 1% Club
programme.desc: Have you ever wondered how clever you are? This is your chance to find out as comedy legend Lee Mack presents the ultimate leveller of a quiz show - it doesn't matter if you're not usually good at quizzes because the questions have nothing to do with remembering facts and are all about logic and common sense. This is the quiz that the whole family can play together - 100 contestants begin every show and try to make it to the end to answer a question that only one per cent of the country can get right and win up to 100,000 pounds.

programme.title: Olivia Attwood: The Price of Perfection
programme.desc: Turkey is the number one destination for Brits seeking cosmetic surgery abroad. Olivia spends six days in the cut price surgery capital of the world, Istanbul, to find out why. She reunites with friend and ex-TOWIE favourite Bobby Norris as he undergoes his first facelift via a celebrity loved concierge service, and meets the CEO to unpack how influencer collaborations power the business. Olivia follows Brits lured by the glossy packages: five star hotels, VIP transfers and dramatic before and afters at a fraction of UK prices. Neelam, a Nottingham receptionist, gets her longed for 'Barbie nose', then discovers how language barriers can complicate recovery. Shelby arrives for 'Turkey teeth' but is stunned by the need for eight root canals. Gemma opts for a full mummy makeover for far less than a UK quote. Olivia weighs up the bargains against the risks.

programme.title: Family Guy
programme.desc: Subversive animated comedy about the trials and tribulations of American family life. After Brian accidentally kills another dog and no-one seems to care, he tries to convince everyone that they should value the life of a dog the same as a human. Lois hires a maid who doesn't listen to Peter.

programme.title: Family Guy
programme.desc: Subversive animated comedy about the everyday trials and tribulations of family life. Stewie offers Brian a demonstration of his latest invention - a device to travel to parallel universes - but things go awry when the baby genius realises that he does not know how to return them to their own universe.

programme.title: Family Guy
programme.desc: Subversive animated comedy about the everyday trials and tribulations of family life. Lois visits the doctor after finding a lump on her breast; although the tests give her the all-clear, her medical history reveals her to be Jewish. Peter is initially keen on the news, but when the ghost of his father visits, he soon changes his mind...

A tussle ensues between them before Geordie is confronted by the realisation that this man is no burglar - he's the new vicar. The man introduces himself as the Reverend Alphy Kottaram - as Alphy settles into life in Grantchester, his first order of business at the church is a funeral service for local landowner Albert Baron, who apparently took his own life - when the service is abruptly interrupted by the Walkers, a family warring with the Barons, a fight breaks out in the church. As the Walkers leave, Albert's son Harvey accuses the Walkers of murdering his father - as Alphy corrals the two families into the vicarage and Geordie arrives to investigate, an initially reluctant Alphy finds himself drawn into solving clues and uncovering buried secrets.

programme.title: Grantchester
programme.desc: Crime drama. Alphy receives a mysterious letter in the post - this is the second time he's received post of its kind, but the meaning behind both letters entirely escapes him. Alphy doesn't have long to dwell on this because he has been invited to Marwood Manor for dinner and a party - Alphy plans to use this opportunity to drum up funds for the ailing church, but when Lady Marwood announces that it's time to play hide and seek, Alphy finds himself opening a cupboard while looking for a suitable hiding spot and is surprised to discover a dead body inside. The body is that of Dennis, the Marwoods' gardener who had apparently left the manor only a day before without a word - a blackmail letter is found on him, but it's not immediately clear whether the letter is addressed to Dennis or if he'd written it for someone else. As Alphy and Geordie investigate the murky world of the manor, they begin to uncover strange secrets and illicit desires amongst the residents and staff there.

programme.title: California Suite
programme.desc: 1978. Comedy. Directed by Herbert Ross. Stars Jane Fonda, Maggie Smith & Michael Caine. The misadventures and struggles of four sets of guests staying at the luxury Beverly Hills Hotel. [S]

programme.title: A Hole Lot of Trouble
programme.desc: Directed by Francis A Searle. A 1969 comedy short centring around workmen digging a hole. Starring Arthur Lowe, Victor Maddern, Bill Maynard and Tim Barrett. [S]

programme.title: Cinebox Memories
programme.desc: Dave Storm and The Diamonds perform the sensational hit 'If You Gotta Make a Fool of Somebody'.

programme.title: The Veil
programme.desc: Girl on the Road. 1958. Stars Boris Karloff, Tod Andrews & Eve Brent. A traveller stops for a stranded young woman on a lonely road and falls for her but their chance meeting is tied in tragedy. [S]

programme.title: Railway Murders
programme.desc: Death on the Underground. 2021. Stars Nicholas Day, Judith Rowbotham & Alan Moss. The murder of 73 year old aristocrat Countess Teresa Lubienska on the eastbound Piccadilly line platform in 1957. [S]

programme.title: Life with the Lyons
programme.desc: 1954. Comedy. Directed by Val Guest. Stars Bebe Daniels, Ben Lyon & Richard Lyon. Ben and Bebe Lyon, along with their family, move into a new home but face some unexpected teething problems. [S]

programme.title: The Captain's Paradise
programme.desc: 1953. Comedy. Directed by Anthony Kimmins. Stars Alec Guinness, Yvonne De Carlo, Celia Johnson & Miles Malleson. The Captain of a ferry boat between Gibraltar & Morocco has a woman in each port. [S]

programme.title: Cinebox Memories
programme.desc: Let's get dancing! Enjoy this fantastic performance from Lionel and Joyce Blair as they dance to the 60s hit 'Must Be Madison'.

programme.title: Grand National Night
programme.desc: 1953. Crime Drama. Directed by Bob McNaught. Stars Nigel Patrick & Moira Lister. A horse trainer's wife unexpectedly dies after a bitter argument, leaving him fearful of being accused of murder. [S]

programme.title: Le Poulet
programme.desc: Le Poulet (The Chicken). 1965. A child becomes attached to a chicken. To stop his parents from eating it, he places an egg near the animal every morning, making it seem like a hen.

programme.title: Orders Are Orders
programme.desc: 1954. Comedy. An American film crew are making a film in a British army camp, but the soldiers chase the film unit's girls. Starring Tony Hancock, Sid James & Peter Sellers. [S]

programme.title: William Tell
programme.desc: The Killer. 1959. Stars: Conrad Phillips, Willoughby Goddard & Jennifer Jayne. Accused of murdering a partisan helper and stealing his gold, Tell must find a way to prove his innocence. [S]

programme.title: Doctor In Distress
programme.desc: 1963. Comedy. Directed by Ralph Thomas. Stars Dirk Bogarde, James Robertson Justice & Samantha Eggar. Dr. Simon Sparrow's love life improves when the lovely Delia Mallory is brought into casualty. [S]

programme.title: Kim Novak: The Golden Age Rebel
programme.desc: 2022. Director: Jessica Menendez. Discover the unforgettable heroine of Hitchcock's masterpiece Vertigo. Explore how the box office sensation takes on the Hollywood system and reclaims her life.

programme.title: Whispering Smith Hits London
programme.desc: 1952. Mystery. Director: Francis Searle. Stars Richard Carlson, Greta Gynt & Herbert Lom. US sleuth Whispering Smith arrives in London on holiday but soon becomes embroiled in a murder case. [S]

programme.title: Litter Defence Volunteers...
programme.desc: ...with Roy Hudd. 1968. The Litter Defence Volunteers stop litter from spoiling the streets, and with more public help they would do even better.

programme.title: Whiplash
programme.desc: Dilemma in Wool. 1961. Stars Peter Graves, Anthony Wickert & Janette Craig. Cobb picks up a woman along with her 'husband' and 'baby'. Cobb soon fears that he is involved in a kidnapping scheme. [S]

programme.title: The Man from U.N.C.L.E
programme.desc: The Foxes and Hounds Affair. 1965. Stars Robert Vaughn, Vincent Price & Patricia Medina. U.N.C.L.E must race against THRUSH to obtain a newly developed mind reading device. [S]

programme.title: Buccaneer
programme.desc: A Kind of Cuckoo. 1980. Stars Bryan Marshall, Shirley Anne Field & Clifford Rose. Monica digs into Burton's past and the new board clashes over control, cash and contracts. [S]

programme.title: Sherlock Holmes: Murder by Decree
programme.desc: 1979. Crime. Director: Bob Clark. Stars: Christopher Plummer, James Mason & David Hemmings. Holmes investigates Jack the Ripper's murders and discovers a conspiracy to protect the killer. [S]

programme.title: Fortean TV
programme.desc: 1997. Hosted by Reverend Lionel Fanthorpe. Tonight, find out what swallowing live fish does for your health, sniff out spirits and reveal exclusive footage of the mythical and mysterious Yeti.

programme.title: The Nudist Story
programme.desc: 1960. Drama. Director: Ramsey Herrington. Stars Shelley Martin, Brian Cobby, Natalie Lynn. A woman is horrified when she inherits a nudist camp but her views are challenged when she falls in love. [S]
